pending.description: Add sap_insert_track(mainWindowHandle, trackIndex, isVideo) to shotcut/src/rustbridge/sap_ffi.cpp wrapping Timeline::InsertTrackCommand (mirrors sap_add_video_track/sap_add_audio_track's AddTrackCommand pattern), returning the resulting track index.
pending.verification: cpp build succeeds; new FFI symbol exported and callable, returns expected index for a manual insert-at-index call.
pending.implementation_evidence: Added sap_insert_track(void*, int trackIndex, int isVideo) in shotcut/src/rustbridge/sap_ffi.cpp (immediately before sap_remove_track, ~line 226) and declared it in shotcut/src/rustbridge/sap_ffi.h (~line 61, after sap_add_audio_track). Deviation from the plan text: it does NOT push Timeline::InsertTrackCommand directly -- it uses TimelineDock::insertVideoTrack()/insertAudioTrack(), which are the dock slots that push that exact command (timelinedock.cpp:2258/2270, InsertTrackCommand(m_model, currentTrack(), Audio|VideoTrackType)). Those slots also clear any live timeline selection first (m_selection.selectedTrack != -1 -> setSelection()), which the add-track path does too and which a raw command push would skip. Since they have no indexed overload, this sets dock->setCurrentTrack(trackIndex) first -- structurally identical to the existing sap_remove_track, whose in-file comment documents the same trick. Same Qt::BlockingQueuedConnection + mainWindowFromHandle + dock->model() null/range checks + syncTimelineProducer(mw) as its neighbours; no new includes needed. Returns trackIndex on success, -1 on error; trackIndex is validated against [0, model->trackList().size()) so appending (and the first track on an empty timeline) must go through sap_add_video_track/sap_add_audio_track -- this deliberately avoids relying on InsertTrackCommand's silent qBound() clamp to rowCount()-1, which would otherwise turn an out-of-range insert into a surprise insert at the last index. STATUS is in_progress, not completed: the cpp could NOT be build-verified here. The shotcut submodule was not even checked out in this worktree (git submodule status showed '-9c5cb36...'); it was cloned locally from the sibling checkout at commit 12a85c6 (the recorded pointer 9c5cb36 does not exist in that clone -- stale) and sap_ffi.cpp/timelinecommands.cpp were diffed byte-for-byte against the sibling working copy before editing. A Qt+MLT build is unavailable in this environment, so correctness rests on pattern-matching against sap_remove_track and the two dock slots. This needs the integration_realsaprust phase's real cpp build to close.

pending.implementation_evidence: ffi.rs: added the sap_insert_track extern "C" declaration after sap_add_audio_track (~line 36). backend.rs: Backend::edit_add_track (trait decl ~line 277) now takes index: Option<usize>; the MockBackend impl (~line 905) validates Some(i) < len (InvalidParams 'index {i} out of range (len {len}); omit index to append'), inserts at that position, then renumbers every Track.index densely and shifts the clips HashMap keys at-or-after the insert point up by one -- the same reindex+remap discipline edit_reorder_track already uses, so listTracks/listClips stay coherent after an insert. index: None keeps the exact previous append path. ffi_backend.rs::edit_add_track (~line 653) now maps kind -> is_video once, then dispatches Some(at) -> ffi::sap_insert_track(handle, at as c_int, is_video as c_int) vs None -> the untouched sap_add_video_track/sap_add_audio_track calls; the kind-validation error, the index < 0 -> InvalidParams check, and the returned Track construction are unchanged. server.rs 'edit.addTrack' handler (~line 427): params struct gained #[serde(default)] index: Option<usize> (camelCase already via serde(rename_all)), passed straight through -- absent and explicit null both mean append. Also migrated 14 pre-existing 2-arg b.edit_add_track("p", "video") call sites in backend.rs's #[cfg(test)] module to pass None. Tests: new tests/server_integration.rs::add_track_index_inserts_and_omitting_it_appends (~lines 234-300) asserts two no-index adds land at 0 then 1, an {kind:audio,index:1} insert returns index 1 and makes listTracks read [video, audio, video] with densely renumbered indices 0/1/2, a subsequent no-index add still appends at 3, and index:9 is rejected with INVALID_PARAMS. pending.description: Add optional index integer param to edit.addTrack in tools_edit.go; document current insertion order (index 0 = topmost) either way.
pending.verification: MCP adapter test: edit.addTrack with index param forwards to sap-rust and inserts at requested position; existing no-index addTrack tests still pass.
pending.implementation_evidence: snapshotd/internal/mcpadapter/tools_edit.go:14 -- edit.addTrack's summary now reads 'appended by default or inserted at an explicit index', plus a new optional mcp.WithInteger("index") whose description states: omit to append (the default, unchanged); a 0-based index of an existing track inserts there and shifts that track and everything after it up by one; the returned Track.index equals the requested value; out-of-range is rejected so the very first track must omit index; and -- stated plainly per the plan -- that index 0 is the TOPMOST timeline track, not the bottom one, so a lower index is a higher video layer. Test: snapshotd/internal/mcpadapter/mcpadapter_test.go:286-360, TestMCPAdapter_AddTrackIndexForwarded, using the package's existing fakeHandler + server.NewTestServer + SSE-client pattern (no real backend). Two subtests: 'index forwarded' calls edit.addTrack{kind:video,index:2} and asserts the dispatched sap method is edit.addTrack with params index==2; 'index omitted' calls {kind:audio} and asserts the dispatched params carry NO index key at all (append is not silently defaulted to 0). Regenerating the committed tool-schema golden was required: snapshotd/docs/schema/snapshotd-mcp.schema.json is asserted byte-equal by TestCommittedSchemaMatchesCurrentTools, so `bash scripts/gen_mcp_schema.sh` was run from snapshotd/ after this and the Phase 1 hexColor description change. CAVEAT for the reviewer: that regeneration swept in PRE-EXISTING golden staleness unrelated to Phases 1-2 -- the committed schema had not been regenerated since 896a96692, so the diff also carries (a) daemon.list gaining a description rewrite, an optional boolean `active` input, and a whole new ~72-line outputSchema; (b) `name` appearing on the Track output object in four places; (c) track.enter gaining a `trackName` param and dropping trackIndex from its `required` array (now []). No Go source behind those three surfaces is dirty in this worktree (git status shows only tools_edit.go, tools_generator_subtitles.go, mcpadapter_test.go), so this is legitimate gen_mcp_schema.sh output against current HEAD, not something these phases introduced -- but it means the schema hunk is larger than Phases 1-2 and may deserve splitting into its own commit.
